item.description: French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. item.title: 'Election without meaningful competition': Russia’s results won't measure support for Putin or war
item.description: Alison Sargent is pleased to welcome Grégoire Roos, Director of the Europe and Russia and Eurasia Programmes at Chatham House. According to Roos, Russia’s parliamentary election is revealing because of what the electoral process can still tell us about the political system Vladimir Putin has constructed. In the absence of any meaningful competition, and anti-war opposition excluded, Roos argues that the most revealing signals may lie elsewhere: in turnout, the timing of voting, the performance of the remaining parties, and the Kremlin’s effort to frame participation itself as evidence of… Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit
item.description: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Early voting begins in US midterms that could see Republicans lose control of Congress
item.description: In-person early voting for the US midterm elections begins Friday, six weeks ahead of the final November 3 vote, which will determine whether Republicans will maintain their majority in the US House and Senate. Some of the main issues American voters are deciding on are how to navigate the cost-of-living crisis, the war in Iran and President Donald Trump’s aggressive immigration enforcement campaign. item.description: Peer takes full-time position at the controversial company as it fends off pressure from both Andy Burnham’s government and Sadiq Khan Another former government minister has been hired by a controversial US AI company, this time Palantir, which has appointed Andy Burnham’s former ministerial colleague Tom Watson. The Labour peer and former deputy leader will operate alongside Palantir’s UK and Europe chief executive, Louis Mosley, as the company attempts to fend off pressure on Burnham’s government to axe its £330m NHS contract . It is also fighting Sadiq Khan in court over the Labour London… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Russia votes in parliamentary election as war in Ukraine drags on
item.description: Polls opened in Russia's Far East on Friday as the country began three days of voting for its parliamentary election, the first since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The Kremlin's main party, United Russia, is poised to keep its grip on power alongside other parties aligned with President Vladimir Putin, as the only party that criticised the war was removed from the ballot. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Bolivia: Parlamento extiende estado de excepción por 90 días
item.description: El Parlamento de Bolivia aprobó la ampliación del estado de excepción por los próximos 90 días, medida establecida originalmente por decreto del presidente Rodrigo Paz. La norma permite al Gobierno movilizar fuerzas militares para contener manifestaciones. Las protestas comenzaron meses atrás debido a la crisis económica y al descontento de los ciudadanos. Informe de nuestra corresponsal, Nathalie Iriarte. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Trump es fotografiado con un cartel sobre la demolición del Kennedy Center en EE. UU.
item.description: Imágenes captadas por un fotógrafo de AFP muestran al presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, a bordo del Air Force One, examinando una copia impresa sobre el Kennedy Center en la que parece leerse la palabra "demolido". La foto se tomó después de que el mandatario advirtiera que el centro de artes escénicas podría ser destruido. Horas más tarde, su Administración alegó ante un tribunal que el recinto debía cerrarse debido a un "deterioro estructural", el último giro en la disputa de Trump por vincular su nombre al edificio. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Macron reúne a Aoun y al rey Abdalá II en París para reforzar el Ejército libanés
item.description: El presidente libanés, Joseph Aoun, y el rey jordano, Abdalá II, se reunieron con el presidente de Francia, Emmanuel Macron, este 17 de septiembre en París, para impulsar el apoyo internacional al Ejército libanés de cara al fin de la misión de la FINUL de la ONU en el sur del Líbano, previsto para diciembre de 2026. Aoun aprovechó el encuentro para abordar con Macron la situación en el sur del país y lo que Beirut califica de continuas "agresiones" israelíes, así como el estado de las negociaciones entre Líbano, Estados Unidos e Israel. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Paz recibe espaldarazo del Congreso para ampliar por 90 días el estado de excepción en Bolivia
item.description: El Congreso de Bolivia aprobó la ampliación del estado de excepción por 90 días, una medida que había sido decretada por el presidente Rodrigo Paz. Este marco legal restringe el derecho a protestar y permite la movilización de militares para mantener el orden público, algo indispensable para evitar los bloqueos viales y proteger la economía, según insistió la Administración. El decreto original entró en vigor el 20 de junio, tras más de 50 días de protestas y bloqueos de carreteras protagonizados por campesinos, indígenas y otros sectores. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: ¿Qué se puede entender por integrante asociado de la UE y por qué Canadá?

item.description: Hong Kong authorities have hit out at a US congressional commission for colluding with “anti-China politicians” to hold a hearing on jailed former media boss Jimmy Lai Chee-ying and introducing a bill to “intimidate” local national security officials with sanctions. item.title: Taking on Trump: Canada and EU forge closer ties – The Latest
item.description: Canadian prime minister, Mark Carney, has welcomed the EU’s proposal for Canada to become the bloc’s first ‘associate member’, despite threats from Donald Trump over the plan. The US president said Washington could impose ‘very serious tariffs’ or halt trade if the EU went ahead with the plan. But in a defiant speech to the European parliament, Carney called for ‘deep cooperation’ and said polling showed the overwhelming majority of Canadians supported closer ties with Europe. Lucy Hough speaks to Europe correspondent Jon Henley – watch on YouTube Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.
